entries.answer: David studies distributed heterogeneous computing, especially ways to make emerging accelerators practical for scientific workloads and the domain scientists who run them. His current work explores scheduling across distributed heterogeneous systems.
David's correlation-compressibility work is available in the FTHPC Correlation_Compressibility repository.

David began his research at Clemson in collaboration with Argonne National Laboratory, developing statistical methods to predict error-bounded lossy compression ratios for scientific data.

entries.answer: The cuNumeric.jl repository is hosted by JuliaLegate on GitHub.

cuNumeric.jl is a Julia array library for running numerical programs across distributed, heterogeneous systems with minimal code changes. Its NDArray type is designed as a drop-in alternative to Julia's standard Array, while the Legate ecosystem uses Legion underneath to organize deferred computations, manage data, and schedule work across resources such as NVIDIA GPUs.

Legion is a task-based runtime for programming distributed, heterogeneous systems. It manages parallel work and data movement across different processors and accelerators. David's work connects to Legion in two ways: cuNumeric.jl uses the Legion-based Legate ecosystem to run array-oriented Julia applications across distributed systems and NVIDIA GPUs, while Legion PIM extends the runtime to support UPMEM Processing-in-Memory accelerators.
The Legion PIM repository is hosted by PrescienceLab on GitHub.

Processing-in-Memory (PIM) places compute capabilities in or near memory so data can be processed without repeatedly moving it to a traditional CPU or GPU. This can reduce the cost and bottleneck of data movement for memory-intensive workloads. David's Legion PIM work integrates UPMEM's PIM processors into the Legion runtime, using Legion to schedule tasks and manage data transfers while making the accelerators easier to program.
David collaborates with Pat McCormick at Los Alamos National Laboratory on scheduling for distributed heterogeneous systems.
David is a recipient of the U.S. Department of Energy Computational Science Graduate Fellowship (DOE CSGF).
